page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration providing high single-core frequency coupled with an unusually large memory footprint. Driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, the instance exposes 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs across an x86_64 architecture. It features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration. The instance is provisioned without local disk storage and contains no dedicated GPU accelerators.

The defining architectural trait of the FX8-4ms_v2 is its memory capacity of 168.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 42.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark results reflect this distinctive design. Single-threaded execution demonstrates exceptional speed, placing in the top 10 percent of Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2351.0, corroborated by strong results in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core metrics like multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation via Clang sit in the lower quartile, limited by the modest four-vCPU count. Memory throughput shows high cache transfer rates of 345.37 GB/sec for 16 KB blocks, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidth drop to 36.1 GB/sec and 25.44 GB/sec respectively.

From an efficiency standpoint, the FX8-4ms_v2 targets workloads constrained by per-core software licensing costs that demand substantial system memory and fast clock speeds rather than wide multi-threaded parallelization. The absence of local ephemeral storage necessitates remote Azure Premium Storage attachments for persistent data handling. The instance serves in-memory database engines, medium-scale Redis deployments, financial transaction modeling, and memory-intensive single-threaded data analytics tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense virtual machine powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it configures 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs alongside 168.0 GB of system memory, providing an uncommon 42.0 GB per vCPU. The processor incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX execution units. Hardware testing reveals top-tier single-core CPU throughput, earning a Geekbench single-core score of 2351.0 and rapid single-threaded decompression metrics, although raw multi-threaded capacity remains bounded by its four vCPUs. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring networked block storage. This profile maximizes cost efficiency for enterprise software requiring per-core licensing with high RAM demands, making it appropriate for in-memory databases, key-value caches like Redis, and memory-heavy sequential batch analytics.
